definition: The Anthropic SDKs are the official client libraries for calling Claude models, including tool use, streaming and vision.
details: Published and maintained by Anthropic for Python and TypeScript/JavaScript.

explainer.lead: How to install Anthropic SDK, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.

quickstart.python:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()   # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
msg = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
    max_tokens=200,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain RLHF in two sentences."}],
)
print(msg.content[0].text)

explainer.inAi: Add a system prompt, pass tools (JSON-schema functions) for agents, or stream tokens to a chat UI.

tiers.eli5: They are ready-made phone lines for talking to Claude from your program.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use the Python or TypeScript/JavaScript library to send requests and handle streamed responses and tool calls. A pitfall is treating SDK defaults as production-ready without managing timeouts and errors.
tiers.paperLevel: Official client libraries published and maintained by Anthropic; they wrap the model API rather than defining model behaviour. Capabilities are bounded by the underlying Claude models.

explainer.example: A Python app imports the SDK to send a prompt with an image and stream the reply back token by token.
